amendments.why: Rule 29 already decides the two-level anarthrous case twice over, and this chapter still read it both ways, because in a multi-level chain the rule's two directions pull opposite: the fronting sentence sends the written the to the article, while the counting direction (read which word each the stands before) sends the inner the to the construct noun standing before it. Four units in this chapter turned on that, and the rule's own levav kol benei haadam -> the hearts of all the children of men settles it: the outer construct takes the supplied second the, so the article takes the one standing before the inner construct's word. The added paragraph states that as a rule and confines the counting direction to the arthrous case it was written for. The rest of the rule is returned unchanged.
amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **But that count governs a rectum the ASV renders arthrously, and a multi-level chain whose innermost rectum is left with no determiner at all is the fronting case, however many constructs stand over it.** Where two or more construct nouns stand over a rectum carrying an article, the ASV writes that rectum with no determiner of its own, and it writes a *the* before more than one of the chain's English nouns, the article's *the* is the one standing before the word of the noun the article's own word immediately depends on, and the outer construct takes the supplied second *the* this rule allows it, the noun between them keeping only its own word and the *of* rule 19 gives it. `אֹצְרוֹת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִים` → *the treasuries of the house of God* gives *the treasuries* to `אוֹצָר`, *the* to the article, *of house* to `בַּיִת` and *of God* to `אֱלֹהִים`, exactly as `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men* gives *the hearts* to the outer construct and the *the* before *children* to the article. Do not read the counting direction above as handing that inner *the* to the construct noun it stands before, which would leave a present article morpheme holding nothing while a written *the* went to a supplied reading, against rule 2 and against the priority rules 46 and 47 give a morpheme that is there. Read the rectum's own determiner first, as the sentences above direct: where the ASV writes a *the* or another determiner before the rectum's own word nothing is fronted and the count governs as before, and where it writes none the article's *the* is fronted one level and this paragraph governs. **And a rectum the ASV renders indefinitely is not an anarthrous one.** Where the article morpheme stands on the rectum, the ASV writes an indefinite article before the rectum's own word, and the phrase's single *the* stands before the construct — `נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם` → *the body of a man* — nothing is fronted: the *a* is that noun's own under rule 15, one word is not determined twice, and the article is `unrepresented` under this rule's last sentence while the construct takes a supplied *the*. What forces fronting is a rectum the ASV leaves with no determiner at all, as `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone* is, so read which determiner stands before the rectum's word before counting the phrase's *the*s. **A construct relation the ASV recasts as an English possessive is not a fronting either.** Where the ASV writes the rectum as a possessive standing before its head noun — `מִלַּת מַלְכָּא` → *the king's matter*, `שַׁלִּיטָא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the king's captain*, `שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's gate* — the *the* at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's own word, because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun. So the article on the rectum takes it and the construct noun keeps only its own word, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one does; supply a *the* on the construct only where the ASV writes a second one, as `רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the captain of the king's guard* does. Do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting: what fronting answers to is an anarthrous rectum, and here the rectum is the very word the *the* determines. **Read that as the determiner of the possessive, not as the word *the*, and read it whether or not the possessor carries an article of its own.** An English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor whatever that determiner is, so an indefinite *a* standing at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's word exactly as a *the* does, and where the possessor's word carries no article morpheme the determiner the ASV supplies still goes to that word rather than to the construct noun: `נְשִׂיא בֵית־אָב` → *a prince of* ***a fathers*** *house* gives *a fathers* to `אָב` and *of ... house* to `בַּיִת`, discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25. This is rule 15's supplied determiner placed by this rule's own reasoning — the noun that licenses an English *a* in such a phrase is the possessor, since *a father's house* is the house of *a* father — and the construct noun takes a determiner of its own only where the ASV writes a second one, on the terms just given. A `דִּי` or other relational morpheme standing between the two nouns is rendered inside the possessive and shares the rectum's unit under rule 30. **And a chain the ASV renders attributively under rule 28 places its supplied determiner on these same terms.** Where the ASV writes the construct noun as an attributive standing before the rectum's own word — `קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו` → *the tall cedars thereof*, `מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו` → *the choice fir trees thereof*, `יְרַק דֶּשֶׁא` → *the green herb*, `בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן` → *The virgin daughter of Zion* — and no article morpheme stands in the phrase, the single written *the* stands before the construct noun's word and that noun takes it as a supplied one, exactly as it does where the same chain is written with *of*. Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that the rectum is the head noun of the English phrase: rule 15's direction to read the noun of the expression rather than its leftmost word governs a numeral and the noun it counts, where the numeral is not a noun the ASV determines at all, and it does not reach a construct chain, whose determiners this rule counts. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as above: where the ASV writes one for each, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, and where an article morpheme stands on the rectum the fronting sentences above govern as before. The unit still heads on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31, so `קוֹמַת` → *the tall* heads on *tall*. **And the same holds where the ASV renders the rectum attributively instead and the construct noun is the English head.** Where the rectum's word stands first and the construct's word after it — `דְּבַר עֶצֶב` → *a grievous word*, `אִישׁ חֵמָה` → *A wrathful man*, `מַחְשְׁבוֹת רָע` → *Evil devices* — and no article morpheme stands in the phrase, the single supplied determiner is still the construct noun's, because what this rule supplies is a determiner on the construct noun and not on whichever of the two words the ASV has put first. Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that it stands before the rectum's word: the counting sentences above weigh the ASV's written determiners against the article morphemes standing in the phrase, and where no article morpheme stands there at all there is nothing to count, so the preceding paragraph's reasoning governs in either English order. Where the ASV writes a determiner for each word, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, as above. Read MACULA's morphology before applying any of this, since rule 15's direction to take the noun of the expression governs a noun with an absolute modifier standing beside it — `לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart*, `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox* — where no construct relation is written and this rule's count does not arise. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.

Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that it stands before the rectum's word: the counting sentences above weigh the ASV's written determiners against the article morphemes standing in the phrase, and where no article morpheme stands there at all there is nothing to count, so the preceding paragraph's reasoning governs in either English order. Where the ASV writes a determiner for each word, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, as above. Read MACULA's morphology before applying any of this, since rule 15's direction to take the noun of the expression governs a noun with an absolute modifier standing beside it — `לֵב שָׂמֵחַ` → *A glad heart*, `שׁוֹר אָבוּס` → *a stalled ox* — where no construct relation is written and this rule's count does not arise. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amended.why: Rule 29 already decides the two-level anarthrous case twice over, and this chapter still read it both ways, because in a multi-level chain the rule's two directions pull opposite: the fronting sentence sends the written the to the article, while the counting direction (read which word each the stands before) sends the inner the to the construct noun standing before it. Four units in this chapter turned on that, and the rule's own levav kol benei haadam -> the hearts of all the children of men settles it: the outer construct takes the supplied second the, so the article takes the one standing before the inner construct's word. The added paragraph states that as a rule and confines the counting direction to the arthrous case it was written for. The rest of the rule is returned unchanged.

report: One real split: the article on a construct chain's nomen rectum where the ASV renders that rectum with no determiner of its own. Eight places give the article the written the and leave the construct bare - 28.14 (kelei hakkesef -> the vessels of silver), 28.15 twice, 28.16 twice, 28.17 twice, 28.18 (mizbach haqqetoret -> the altar of incense). Four places instead mark the article unrepresented and supply a the on the construct - 28.1 sarei haalafim -> the captains of thousands and sarei hammeoth -> the captains of hundreds, 28.12 otzroth beith haelohim, 28.21 avodath beith haelohim. Nothing in the source licenses the difference; rule 29 settles it for the article, which is unrepresented only where the ASV writes no the for the chain at all. Patched 1CH.28.1, 1CH.28.12, 1CH.28.21.

28.12 and 28.21 are three-level chains carrying two written the's. Rule 29's multi-level clause gives the supplied second the to the outer construct (otzar, avodah), so the article takes the the standing before the inner construct's word and bayith keeps only of house - the division of the rule's own levav kol benei haadam -> the hearts of all the children of men. The competing reading, which hands that the to bayith under the rule's counting direction, is named in each unit's note; the pull between those two directions is what the amendment to rule 29 removes.

The chapter's arthrous chains were already reading the same way and are untouched: machleqoth hakkohanim -> the courses of the priests (28.13, 28.21), beith hakkapporeth -> the place of the mercy seat (28.11), tavnith hammerkavah -> the pattern of the chariot (28.18). haelohim amar -> God said at 28.3 stays unrepresented, no the being written for that phrase at all, and the agreement articles of 28.7 and 28.8 stay unrepresented under rules 41 and 47.

Nothing else in the 49-lemma table is a split. The waw connectives (and, but, Then, Howbeit, even, also, therefore) are read off the ASV under rule 14; every lamed rendered or unrendered turns on whether the ASV writes a word for it (rules 40, 52); bayith, sar, avodah, zahav and mishqal vary in English only. The two ad-lamed pairs (28.7 for, 28.20 until) both fuse under rule 30 headed on ad, as rule 23 directs.

Read the added units end to end, since the table is blind to them. The three appositional even's (28.18, 28.19, 28.20) are all added with no marker and no conjunction in the clause, while 28.1's even goes to a waw that is written - a difference the source licenses. The four supplied objects (me at 28.4, it at 28.8, 28.10, 28.20) are all added under rule 44. The italic runs (of the temple, vessels of, of silver, silver, their wings, said David) are each one unit under rule 2. The distributive repetitions at 28.14-17 are uniform: first occurrence takes the noun with its supplied determiner, the waw and the repeated noun unrepresented.

BSB: of the seven Td disagreements, four (28.1 twice, 28.12, 28.21) are the split above and are now represented, so the reference alignment corroborated the finding. The other three (28.3, 28.7, 28.8) are correct as they stand. The R, C and Ncfsa disagreements are the documented rule 40, 14 and 22 conventions - unrendered prepositions, unrendered waws, and the second half of a distributive repetition - and none is an error.
